articles.title: Mindre kolanvändning i USA sänker utsläppen
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Mindre kolanvändning i USA sänker utsläppen
articles.body_text: Minskad kolanvändning i USA drar ned utsläppen, enligt nya beräkningar. Arkivbild Mindre kolanvändning i USA sänker utsläppen Koldioxidutsläppen från energisektorn i USA väntas minska något under 2026. En avgörande faktor är att landets kraftverk använder mindre kol, visar en analys gjord av forskningsinstitutet Energy Innovation. Utvecklingen står i kontrast mot 2025, då utsläppen från USA:s energisektorn vände uppåt. Minskad konsumtion av bensin och diesel bidrar också, medan användningen av fossil gas går i sidled, enligt Energy Innovation. Enligt institutets beräkningar ser det ut som att utsläppen från USA:s energisektor i år hamnar 70 miljoner ton under 2025 års nivå, en nedgång på cirka 2 procent. Totalt beräknas – utifrån federal statistik för perioden januari–juli och prognoser för resten av året – koldioxidutsläppen från energisektorn i USA till 4,85 miljarder ton.

articles.title: Chockhöjd turkisk inflationsprognos
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Chockhöjd turkisk inflationsprognos
articles.body_text: Turkiets centralbank höjer prognosen för prisökningar i år och nästa år. Arkivbild Turkiets centralbank chockhöjer sin prognos för inflationen med hänvisning till effekter av Irankriget och marknadsturbulens. Inflationen – det vill säga konsumentprisökningarna i årstakt – väntas nu ligga på 21 procent i slutet av 2027, vilket kan jämföras med en tidigare prognos på 15 procent. Inflationsprognosen för slutet av 2026 höjs också, till 29,5 procent från tidigare 28,0 procent. Turkiet importerar i princip all olja och gas som konsumeras i landet. Den turkiska ekonomin skakas även av problem med stora fonder, där nästan en halv miljon sparare har drabbats när 131 fonder likviderats. Krisen har bland annat tvingat centralbanken att göra stödköp av obligationer för att stabilisera marknaden. Turkiets centralbank sänkte i oktober styrräntan med 1 procentenhet till 36 procent.

articles.title: Indisk inflation lyfter mer än väntat
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Indisk inflation lyfter mer än väntat
articles.body_text: Oväntat snabbt stigande priser i Indien. Arkivbild. Inflationen i Indien – världens största land räknat i antal invånare – stiger mer än väntat. Inflationen i oktober uppmättes till 6,1 procent, upp från 5,5 procent i oktober. Snittprognosen bland analytiker låg på 6,0 procent. Den indiska centralbanken har 2–6 procent som tolererbart spann som sitt inflationsmål. Matpriserna i Indien steg 8,9 procent i årstakt i oktober, visar torsdagens inflationsrapport. Detta var mer än i september, då matpriserna steg 7,7 procent. Landet påverkas bland annat av väderfenomenet El Niño, som gjort att vattenreservoarerna är ovanligt låga och som även bromsar de indiska skördevolymerna.

articles.title: Rapportrally för trenchcoat-klassikern
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Rapportrally för trenchcoat-klassikern
articles.body_text: Basketlaget Oklahoma City Thunder poserar i trenchcoats från Burberry. Arkivbild Satsningen på sänkta priser av modehuset Burberry – med sina klassiska trenchcoats och halsdukar – har gett klirr i kassan, visar en kvartalsrapport. På Londonbörsen är det klackarna i taket, med ett kurslyft på som mest 10 procent i förmiddagshandeln efter rapporten. Vd Joshua Schulmans strategi bygger sedan två år på att flirta med mer prismedvetna lyxkonsumenter med sänkta priser, personalneddragningar och tydligare fokus på Burberrys klassiska halsdukar och trenchcoats i gabardin. Bland annat har det gett tillväxt i Kina, där marknaden för exklusiva kläder i övrigt bromsar.

articles.title: Återköpsprogram ger kurslyft för Rolls-Royce
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Återköpsprogram ger kurslyft för Rolls-Royce
articles.body_text: Rolls-Royce ökar takten på återköp av aktier med 20 miljarder kronor. Arkivbild Återköpsprogram ger kurslyft för Rolls-Royce Aktien i den brittiska försvars- och verkstadskoncernen Rolls-Royce lyfter med nästan 4 procent. Ett besked om ett nytt program för återköp av aktier – en sorts utdelning till ägarna – på 1,5 miljarder pund (cirka 20 miljarder kronor) – tolkas positivt av investerare. Rolls-Royce aktie har sedan årsskiftet gått upp 19 procent och ser enligt analytikern David H Perry på JP Morgan ”exceptionellt attraktiv” ut.

articles.title: Publicistiska grunden för journalistik på TV4
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4?
articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. articles.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Ukraine talks with Vladimir Putin
articles.summary: Later on Thursday, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Dublin to meet Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.
articles.body_text: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, a day after the latest talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi. Videos shared by Russian media showed Kushner and Witkoff disembarking a plane and being welcomed by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev with handshakes and hugs. The American negotiatiors were due to meet Putin at 12:00 local time (09:00 GMT), and will then fly to Dublin to speak to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. On Tuesday, Kushner said the US had seen "some openings and some opportunities" and that they would try to "make some progress" at the meeting with Putin. The in-person talks with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents were only announced on Wednesday after two days of talks which were framed as centred around the postwar security architecture of Europe. Nearly five years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow shows no sign of backing down from its maximalist demands for sovereign Ukrainian territory and for Western countries to give up any future commitment to protecting Kyiv in case of further attacks. During the first years of the war, Europeans cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly. However, in recent times many have grown concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin, and have been pushing for a seat at the negotiating table. The talks in Abu Dhabi were led by the Americans and only included Russia and Ukraine, but Kushner said he and Witkoff would ask Putin to "give his blessing" to invite European representatives in future discussions - particularly with regards to the future configuration of their continent's security architecture. Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations. But the Russians have been opposed to the idea, citing Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle. Vladimir Medinsky, who headed the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi, said he thought all parties had "moved closer to achieving peace" but that now "a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the United States, and on whether Europe comes to its senses".

articles.title: British woman missing from cruise ship in Atlantic
articles.summary: The 72-year-old was last seen aboard the Tui ship on Monday as it headed towards the Caribbean.
articles.body_text: A British woman has gone missing from a cruise ship while it was crossing the Atlantic, travel operator Tui has said. The 72-year-old was last seen aboard Tui's Marella Voyager on Monday while the vessel was en route to the Caribbean. The ship could have travelled hundreds of miles in the time between when she was last seen to when she was reported missing. Staff realised the passenger was missing on Tuesday, when they noticed her bed had not been slept in. The alarm was raised and a search carried out, Tui said in a statement. It is understood the missing guest was then reported to the US Coast Guard, which asked the ship to continue to its crossing rather than reverse course and search for the woman. Holidaymakers were told to abandon dinners, drinks and entertainment as the crew carried out an emergency headcount on Tuesday evening, the Daily Mail reports. Passengers stood in lines of four while staff scanned boarding cards to verify the identity of every person on the ship, according to the newspaper. The USCG Rescue Co-ordination Centre in Norfolk, Virginia has issued an alert calling on any ships nearby to "keep a sharp look out" for the woman, the Mail reports. The BBC has contacted the USCG for comment. The Marella Voyager, carrying around 2,000 passengers and 800 crew, left Malaga on 4 November and is due to arrive in Antigua on Friday before calling at Dominica and finishing its voyage in Barbados on Sunday. A spokeswoman for Marella Cruises said it was "deeply saddened" by the disappearance, adding: "Our thoughts are with the guest's loved ones at this very difficult time. "We're supporting the authorities with their enquiries, and out of respect for the guest and their family, we won't be commenting further at this stage." A UK Foreign Office spokesperson said: "We are supporting the family of a British national reported missing on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean and we are in touch with the relevant authorities." In a separate case, a cruise ship pianist was found treading water on Sunday around 20 miles off the Californian coast after falling overboard.

articles.title: Kampala school deaths: Ugandan police investigate suspected poisoning
articles.summary: The girls started vomiting after eating oranges brought in by a fellow pupil - police are travelling to the village they came from.
articles.body_text: Ugandan police are investigating the deaths of four pupils at a school in the capital Kampala which they suspect may be the result of poisoning. The four girls, aged between nine and 11 years, died on Tuesday. Three of the pupils died at home while the fourth passed away while receiving emergency treatment at a hospital. The head teacher at the school, Ta'aliim Primary School and Quran Memorisation Centre, has been arrested to assist with investigations. According to the school, eight pupils had eaten oranges shared by a fellow pupil. Five pupils, including the four who later died, started vomiting. The fifth is still in hospital. Post-mortem examinations are being carried out to determine the exact cause of death. A police spokesperson was quoted by local media as saying that detectives would visit the village where the oranges the pupils ate came from. The centre has been cordoned off as a crime scene. Ugandan media shared videos of grieving parents describing their children's final moments, with some accusing the school of failing to provide clear and timely information. The police have offered condolences to the bereaved families and affected community and say more information will be provided in due course. The tragedy comes at a time when concerns are mounting over health and safety conditions in schools across Uganda. Previous cases involving suspected contaminated food and exposure to harmful substances have left pupils hospitalised with symptoms including stomach pain, vomiting and breathing difficulties.

articles.title: Ukraine's power supply close to critical as Russian strikes bring darkness and cold
articles.summary: For parents in parts of Ukraine, trying to lead a normal family life with just a few hours of power each day is taking its toll.
articles.body_text: Daryna Kulchytska is a mum under pressure. A single parent in a seventh floor flat in Kyiv trying to feed two lively kids and ensure they do their homework. But Daryna also faces the added strain of a deadline she can't even be certain of. All she knows is soon the lights will go out, the sockets will lose power, the wi-fi will drop, and the taps will run dry. Tonight, the electricity has kept flowing an hour longer than advertised, but Daryna's still racing to serve dinner and finish her own work from home. "The last few days it was only four or five hours we had power, but it's not at the same times. For two hours we have electricity, then for eight hours we don't." As peace talks continue, with US envoys meeting the Russian and Ukrainian leaders on Thursday, Ukrainians are facing a rolling schedule of planned power cuts because of intensified Russian attacks on their energy grid. Ukraine has responded by striking Russian oil refineries. Officials are concerned that life will quickly become unsustainable for millions of Ukrainians if power supplies cannot be maintained for at least four hours per day. Some privately warn that's close already, as some families are living with outages of up to 20 hours in Kyiv. The power cuts were introduced earlier this year than last winter, and they're already lasting longer - making homes like Daryna's darker and colder. She's wrapped in layers of clothing and a heavy coat - the temperature is dropping, indoors and out. Just before 7:30pm, there's a click and that's it - darkness until dawn. The lift doesn't work, the water will stop flowing because electricity is needed to pump it to their flat. So the torches and LED candles come out and Daryna, her son Kyryll and daughter Olena gather for a card game of Uno before an early night. Twelve-year-old Kyryll, speaking perfect English learned during two years living in the US, is frank about the disruption. "There's no light, no water, no heat, no electricity. And no fun. All the fun got sucked out with the electricity," he says. "We have a lot of board games. We have a whole shelf, but we've played them like a hundred thousand times already." Many families sit in the shadows as blackouts sweep entire neighbourhoods, smothering homes and streets in darkness. "You look outside and sometimes you see nothing. You have a big city around but you see nothing because there's no light," Daryna says.

articles.title: New York building collapse kills at least four people
articles.summary: A dangerous search for survivors continues after a three-storey building collapsed in Brooklyn on Wednesday afternoon.
articles.body_text: At least four people have died after a building in New York City collapsed into an open construction site on Wednesday afternoon. Nineteen others have been injured, of whom four are in a critical condition, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News, which cited local officials. The collapse sparked a massive search-and-rescue operation, with more than 250 first responders going to the scene of the fallen three-storey building in Brooklyn. Aerial footage has shown firefighters pulling a survivor, covered in dust, out of the debris on a stretcher. She was later said to have been a pregnant woman. Officials previously said they did not know how many others are missing. The BBC has contacted the New York City Fire Department (FDNY) for further comment. An investigation is under way into what caused the sudden collapse. Witnesses described a terrifying sound as the building came down at about 16:00 local time (21:00 GMT). "I live literally right behind the building," one woman, Emmanuella Carilus, told the New York Times. "It sounded like a big boom and you just heard a bunch of screaming." The newspaper published images showing a crowd of fire trucks and police vehicles at the same, and wrote that the noise of sirens had not stopped in the area. "I've never seen anything like this," said another witness, named only as Dashik, who spoke to local television station PIX 11. Officials are yet to identify those who died or were injured. Locals have gathered at the scene to await news of those feared to have been caught in the collapse.

articles.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
articles.summary: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
articles.body_text: At least six people have been killed and about 20 injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital, the biggest in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says. Eyewitnesses told the BBC that a single missile fired by a warplane hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units overnight. The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizk Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions". The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces. Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime". Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war. Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies. Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory. In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said the missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department. A spokesman for the Civil Defence, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry, initially said that five people had been killed and 20 others injured. Videos shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by the blast. Local activists have also circulated claims that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building.

articles.title: Australian teen missing in bush for six days rescued alive
articles.summary: The 17-year-old's mum has joked that he is "grounded for life" and "never leaving the house again".
articles.body_text: A teenager missing for six days in dense Australian bushland has been found alive. William, whose surname has not been released, disappeared last Friday while on a camping trip with a friend in bushland about 180km (112 miles) east of Melbourne, Victoria. Extremely cold overnight temperatures had left authorities concerned for the 17-year-old's welfare. Police dogs, divers and helicopters had been involved in the search. He was located on Thursday morning and reunited with his relieved family, who said he was uninjured but "grounded for life". Rescuers winched William to safety, and fed him a doughnut and a bottle of water, before he was taken to hospital for a check up. The boy's mother, Elizabeth Barkley, told reporters the teenager had "only a few scratches" and seemed fit and healthy. "He's doing fine, everything seems to be fine, he's in perfect health," she added. "He just stayed in one spot and waited to be rescued and I'm just over the moon he's alive." Joking, she added: "He's never leaving the house again." Police have said officers were emotional to have found the teen alive. "It doesn't happen all the time," Victoria Police Acting Inspector Jason Benbow said. "I'm sure he's got a story to tell us soon, which we're very keen to hear," he added.

articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom makes history as Mississippi's first black senator since 19th Century
articles.summary: In a state Trump won two years ago by 22 points, Colom's victory extends a string of Democratic wins in the Senate.
articles.body_text: Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades. Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be seated in the US Senate since Blanche Bruce served from 1875 to 1881. Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called. Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote. Hyde-Smith, who received 48.7%, congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well. "While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said. Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky. Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election. "They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said. "It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did." "In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference." Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced.

articles.summary: Following a ceremony marking Veterans Day, a group that included Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth was shouted at to be quiet.

The incident followed a wreath-laying ceremony marking Veterans Day. Hegseth had joined the group for a photo and someone laughed, prompting the US Army sentinel guarding the tomb to shout. "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times", the sentinel said. According to the BBC's US partner, CBS News, the people in the photo before the reprimand also included Hegseth's advisers Patrick Weaver and Tami Radabaugh, Hegseth's chief of staff Ricky Buria and Hegseth's wife Jennifer Hegseth. "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement. articles.title: Famed ship SS United States deliberately sunk off Florida coast to become a reef
articles.summary: Activists wanted the historic liner to be turned into a museum, but it will instead become the world's largest artificial ocean reef.
articles.body_text: A ship that was once the fastest in the world and is longer than the Titanic has intentionally been sunk off the coast of Florida, turning into the world's largest artificial ocean reef. The SS United States spent nearly 30 years docked in Philadelphia before it was moved to Florida, where it will become a home for sealife and an underwater attraction for marine enthusiasts. Activists unsuccessfully fought for the historic liner - which crossed the Atlantic Ocean hundreds of times - to be preserved as a museum. Instead, after being purchased by a Florida county, it was added to the dozens of artificial reefs off the coast, with a land-based museum detailing the ship's history also planned. Before its retirement, the SS United States was known for carrying royalty and celebrities between the US and Europe, beginning in 1952 and ending in 1969. A young Bill Clinton, before he was president, used the ship to cross the Atlantic. Former presidents Harry Truman, Dwight Eisenhower and John Kennedy also travelled on the vessel. The ship was moved from Philadelphia to Alabama last year for cleaning and remediation work. On Monday, it took its final journey from Alabama to the coast of Destin, Florida, where it was sunk on Wednesday in a precision operation without explosives. Stars including Marlon Brando, Coco Chanel, Duke Ellington, Salvador Dali, Walt Disney, Judy Garland and Cary Grant also boarded the ship during its sailing lifetime. Before its purchase by the municipal Florida government, a number of proposals that would have seen the ship live a second life as a museum or a floating hotel failed. Instead, it sat at various docks with various owners as legal battles played out. The SS United States Conservancy group repeatedly attempted to keep the ship above water, but was unsuccessful.

articles.title: Gibran Rakabuming Raka: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
articles.summary: The news comes at a turbulent time for President Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.
articles.body_text: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka tendered his resignation to parliament on Thursday, triggering the process of finding his replacement amid growing turmoil for the government. Gibran had been facing impeachment calls after a Supreme Court ruling that a high-school document used during his 2024 election campaign was invalid. His departure comes amid a faltering political alliance between his father, ex-president Joko Widodo, and the incumbent President Prabowo Subianto. Standing alongside Gibran, Prabowo told reporters he had accepted his resignation with "a heavy heart". Upper house lawmakers will have 60 days to fill the vacancy from two candidates nominated by the president. "[Gibran] has demonstrated a chivalrous attitude, a strong sense of responsibility, and the qualities of a statesman," Prabowo said, adding that the resignation was "for the benefit of the nation, the state, and the people of Indonesia". "He certainly believes that he completed his education through a proper and structured process. However, we must understand that educational systems abroad differ from those in Indonesia," the president said. Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office. Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials. Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated. "No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said. It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion. The Supreme Court ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.

articles.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
articles.summary: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
articles.body_text: Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store. The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there." She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said. Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

articles.summary: Real Madrid player Vinícius Jr sent a surprise message to 13-year-old fan Zaher who lost both his legs after being hit by a drone in Khartoum, in 2024.

Zaher lost both his legs after a drone strike in Khartoum, Sudan, where the battle between Sudan's army and the RSF continues to devastate the country. After surgery followed by months of physiotherapy and psychological support in Cairo, Zehar returned to Sudan feeling "uplifted" by Vini Jr's message he says. articles.title: Israel bombardea el hospital Nasser en Gaza y deja seis muertos y más de 20 heridos
articles.summary: El ejército de Israel confirmó que el bombardeo en Jan Yunis tenía como objetivo a un alto responsable de Hamás y otros integrantes de su brazo armado que, según su versión, operaban desde el hospital Nasser en Gaza
articles.body_text: Seis personas murieron y al menos 20 resultaron heridas este jueves en un ataque israelí contra el hospital Nasser, en Jan Yunis, en el sur de la Franja de Gaza, según los servicios de emergencia del territorio palestino. El ejército israelí confirmó haber llevado a cabo un bombardeo que tenía como objetivo a “un alto responsable de Hamás y otros miembros de la rama armada del movimiento” islamista que operaban desde ese centro médico. “El saldo del ataque israelí en el interior del complejo médico Nasser (...) subió a seis muertos”, aseguró a la AFP la Defensa Civil, una organización de primeros auxilios que opera bajo la autoridad de Hamás, y agregó que más de 20 personas habían resultado heridas. El hospital confirmó los seis fallecimientos en un comunicado. El portavoz del movimiento palestino, Hazem Qasem, denunció un “crimen de guerra”. En el centro de la Franja de Gaza, la Defensa Civil también informó de la muerte de un palestino, abatido por “disparos israelíes” al este del campo de refugiados de Al Bureij, lo que elevó a siete el número de muertos registrados “desde el amanecer”. Israel y Hamás se acusan mutuamente de violar el alto el fuego que entró en vigor el 10 de octubre de 2025, tras dos años de guerra desencadenada por el ataque sin precedentes del movimiento islamista palestino en territorio israelí el 7 de octubre de 2023. Más de 1.600 palestinos han muerto desde la entrada en vigor del alto fuego, según el Ministerio de Sanidad de Gaza, bajo la autoridad de Hamás, cuyos datos son considerados fiables por la ONU.

articles.title: ¿Cuáles son los días NO laborables por la visita del papa León XIV en Perú?
articles.summary: Visita del papa León XIV en Perú: ¿qué días serán no laborables en Lima, Callao, Chiclayo, Cusco y Pucallpa? El Gobierno peruano estableció días no laborables compensables en distintas regiones del país para facilitar el desplazamiento de la población y su participación en las actividades programadas por la visita del papa León XIV. Todos los detalles, en esta nota.
articles.body_text: Luego de que el Vaticano informara sobre la recuperación favorable del papa León XIV tras una intervención quirúrgica por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, muchas instituciones y organizaciones continúan con la preparación para su visita al Perú. De hecho, el Gobierno nacional estima que la visita del Santo Padre al país podría movilizar a unas 854 000 personas, entre ellas más de 50 000 turistas extranjeros, quienes buscarán acercarse a él para recibir su bendición. Por ello, el Ejecutivo busca facilitar la participación de la población en las actividades que desarrollará el pontífice en las regiones que visitará, por lo que estableció días no laborables. Esta medida permitirá que los ciudadanos puedan asistir a los encuentros programados con Robert Prevost; sin embargo, las horas dejadas de trabajar deberán ser recuperadas posteriormente. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. A través del Decreto Supremo n.º 020-2026-TR, el Gobierno estableció días no laborables entre el 11 al 16 de noviembre para Lima, Callao, Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Piura, Cusco y Ucayali, con motivo a la visita del papa León XIV. Esta medida es compensable y se rige por normas distintas a las de los feriados. Es decir, en el sector público, las horas no laboradas deben recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores o en el plazo que establezca cada entidad. En tanto, en el sector privado, empleadores y trabajadores pueden acordar la forma de compensar esas horas. Si no llegan a un consenso, el empleador determina las condiciones para su recuperación. Por consiguiente, te presentamos, compartido por Infobae, los departamentos en las que regirá estos días de descanso: 11 de noviembre: 12 de noviembre: 13 de noviembre: 14 de noviembre: 15 de noviembre: 16 de noviembre: Durante su visita al Perú, el papa León XIV participará en una vigilia de oración junto a miles de jóvenes de entre 16 y 35 años, que se realizará el jueves 12 de noviembre, a las 6:00 p. m., en el Estadio Nacional. Asimismo, el lunes 16 presidirá la Santa Misa de clausura, programada para las 10:30 a. m. en la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Según los organizadores, los asistentes deberán contar con una entrada gratuita, que podrán obtener a través de las plataformas Teleticket y Ticketmaster. Sin embargo, quienes no puedan asistir a alguna de estas actividades por diversos motivos no podrán ceder su entrada a un familiar o ser querido, ya que los boletos son intransferibles y están vinculados a los datos personales registrados previamente por cada asistente, según informó el Arzobispado de Lima. Inclusive, indicaron que será indispensable presentar el documento de identidad en la puerta del recinto el día del evento, garantizando que el acceso sea gratuito.

articles.title: El papa León XIV se despide de Argentina: “Me he sentido como en casa”
articles.summary: León XIV se despide de Argentina y expresa su gratitud por la acogida de los fieles durante su visita apostólica.
articles.body_text: “Gracias por recibirme con tanto cariño, me he sentido como en casa”, así se despidió este miércoles León XIV de Argentina tras celebrar una misa ante dos millones de fieles en el santuario de Nuestra Señora de Luján. “Queridos hermanos y hermanas: doy gracias a Dios por lo vivido en mi visita a este país, cuna de nuestro querido papa Francisco. Agradezco a todos los que trabajaron para que esto fuera posible”, dijo el papa estadounidense y peruano antes de viajar a Perú para la última etapa de su gira por Latinoamérica. articles.title: ¿El mes de noviembre tiene feriados? Revisa cuáles son los días NO laborables en Perú
articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. El calendario contempla las siguientes fechas: La compensación dependerá del sector laboral. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. Si no consiguen llegar a un consenso, el empleador establecerá las condiciones para realizar la compensación correspondiente. Aunque ambas fechas permiten interrumpir las actividades habituales, tienen condiciones distintas. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. En cambio, los días no laborables suelen estar dirigidos principalmente al sector público y contemplan la recuperación posterior del tiempo pendiente. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. Las sanciones económicas varían según el tipo de empresa, y pueden ir desde poco más de 1.000 soles hasta superar los 24.000.

Por ello, el Ejecutivo busca facilitar la participación de la población en las actividades que desarrollará el pontífice en las regiones que visitará, por lo que estableció días no laborables. Esta medida permitirá que los ciudadanos puedan asistir a los encuentros programados con Robert Prevost; sin embargo, las horas dejadas de trabajar deberán ser recuperadas posteriormente. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. A través del Decreto Supremo n.º 020-2026-TR, el Gobierno estableció días no laborables entre el 11 al 16 de noviembre para Lima, Callao, Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Piura, Cusco y Ucayali, con motivo a la visita del papa León XIV. Esta medida es compensable y se rige por normas distintas a las de los feriados. Asimismo, el lunes 16 presidirá la Santa Misa de clausura, programada para las 10:30 a. m. en la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Según los organizadores, los asistentes deberán contar con una entrada gratuita, que podrán obtener a través de las plataformas Teleticket y Ticketmaster. Sin embargo, quienes no puedan asistir a alguna de estas actividades por diversos motivos no podrán ceder su entrada a un familiar o ser querido, ya que los boletos son intransferibles y están vinculados a los datos personales registrados previamente por cada asistente, según informó el Arzobispado de Lima. articles.body_text: El precio del dólar cerró este miércoles en S/3,409 en el mercado interbancario peruano, por debajo de los S/3,413 de la jornada anterior, con una caída de 0,12%. El sol logró apreciarse pese al fortalecimiento de la moneda estadounidense a nivel internacional, impulsado por las expectativas de nuevas alzas de tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal (Fed) ante la persistencia de las presiones inflacionarias. “El Índice del Dólar Estadounidense (DXY) avanzó 0,66%, hasta los 102.889 puntos, mientras el mercado asigna una probabilidad cercana al 87% a un incremento de 25 puntos básicos en las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal en diciembre. Este escenario fortalece al dólar frente a sus principales pares, aunque el sol peruano logró mantener una ligera apreciación durante la jornada”, explicó Jorge Luis Huayta, trader FX de Kambista. En los mercados internacionales, el oro retrocedió 0,97%, hasta US$3,992.66 por onza, mientras la plata avanzó 0,80% y el cobre subió 0,19%. Por su parte, el petróleo WTI aumentó 1,22%, hasta US$87,09 por barril. Wall Street también registró ganancias, con un avance de 2.87% en el Nasdaq 100, de 1,63% en el S&P 500 y de 0,40% en el Dow Jones. En América Latina, el peso colombiano se apreció 0,72% y el real brasileño ganó 0,39%. En el mercado local, el tipo de cambio fluctuó entre S/3,408 y S/3,413, con un volumen negociado de US$262.7 millones. La cotización mantuvo una tendencia bajista durante la sesión, en contraste con el avance del dólar frente a otras monedas internacionales, como el euro, que retrocedió 0,65%, la libra esterlina (-0,49%) y el yen japonés (-0,70%). De cara a las próximas jornadas, el análisis de Kambista señala que las expectativas sobre las decisiones de la Reserva Federal y la evolución de los precios de los metales seguirán siendo factores relevantes para el comportamiento del dólar frente al sol. En el ámbito local, la atención estará centrada en la decisión de política monetaria del Banco Central de Reserva (BCR), prevista para este jueves 12 de noviembre, que podría ofrecer nuevas señales sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés en el país.

articles.summary: El calendario peruano de 2026 contempla fechas especiales durante noviembre. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan este mes, qué días se celebran y si habrá jornadas de descanso para los trabajadores del sector público y privado.
articles.body_text: Los días libres son una oportunidad para compartir tiempo en familia, organizar actividades personales o realizar pequeños viajes sin las obligaciones habituales del trabajo. En noviembre de 2026, el calendario peruano contempla fechas de descanso que deben distinguirse entre feriados nacionales y días no laborables establecidos de manera extraordinaria. Estas últimas disposiciones están vinculadas con la visita del papa León XIV al Perú y comprenden jornadas y horarios específicos en Lima, Callao y otras regiones del país. Además, no todos los trabajadores tendrán las mismas condiciones para acceder a estos descansos, pues algunas medidas requieren compensar posteriormente las horas que se dejen de trabajar. Conoce qué fechas están previstas para noviembre, en qué lugares se aplicarán y cuáles son las diferencias que debes tener en cuenta antes de organizar tus actividades. El calendario de noviembre tiene un feriado nacional, el pasado 1 de noviembre, día de todos los santos, sin embargo; también cuenta con días NO laborables según lo indica la ley. Estas últimas fueron oficializadas mediante el Decreto Supremo N.º 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario oficial El Peruano. En las entidades públicas, las horas pendientes deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores al descanso o cuando lo determine el titular de cada institución, de acuerdo con las necesidades del servicio. En las empresas privadas, empleadores y trabajadores podrán acordar cómo reponer el tiempo no trabajado. El feriado constituye un descanso obligatorio reconocido por ley y no requiere recuperar las horas que correspondían a esa jornada. Para los trabajadores privados, su aplicación depende del acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Según la Cámara de Comercio de Lima (CCL), si un empleado trabaja en un día feriado debido a necesidades de la empresa o rotación de turnos, y no recibe un día libre en sustitución, debe recibir una compensación económica equivalente a tres veces su salario habitual por esa jornada laboral. Esto se debe a tres conceptos: No cumplir con el pago adicional o negar la compensación de descanso constituye una infracción muy grave en materia laboral. articles.body_text: Seis personas murieron y al menos 20 resultaron heridas este jueves en un ataque israelí contra el hospital Nasser, en Jan Yunis, en el sur de la Franja de Gaza, según los servicios de emergencia del territorio palestino. El ejército israelí confirmó haber llevado a cabo un bombardeo que tenía como objetivo a “un alto responsable de Hamás y otros miembros de la rama armada del movimiento” islamista que operaban desde ese centro médico. “El saldo del ataque israelí en el interior del complejo médico Nasser (...) subió a seis muertos”, aseguró a la AFP la Defensa Civil, una organización de primeros auxilios que opera bajo la autoridad de Hamás, y agregó que más de 20 personas habían resultado heridas. Israel y Hamás se acusan mutuamente de violar el alto el fuego que entró en vigor el 10 de octubre de 2025, tras dos años de guerra desencadenada por el ataque sin precedentes del movimiento islamista palestino en territorio israelí el 7 de octubre de 2023. articles.summary: Visita del papa León XIV en Perú: ¿qué días serán no laborables en Lima, Callao, Chiclayo, Cusco y Pucallpa? El Gobierno peruano estableció días no laborables compensables en distintas regiones del país para facilitar el desplazamiento de la población y su participación en las actividades programadas por la visita del papa León XIV. Todos los detalles, en esta nota.
articles.body_text: Luego de que el Vaticano informara sobre la recuperación favorable del papa León XIV tras una intervención quirúrgica por un adenocarcinoma pulmonar, muchas instituciones y organizaciones continúan con la preparación para su visita al Perú. De hecho, el Gobierno nacional estima que la visita del Santo Padre al país podría movilizar a unas 854 000 personas, entre ellas más de 50 000 turistas extranjeros, quienes buscarán acercarse a él para recibir su bendición. Por ello, el Ejecutivo busca facilitar la participación de la población en las actividades que desarrollará el pontífice en las regiones que visitará, por lo que estableció días no laborables. Esta medida permitirá que los ciudadanos puedan asistir a los encuentros programados con Robert Prevost; sin embargo, las horas dejadas de trabajar deberán ser recuperadas posteriormente. En la siguiente nota te contamos todo lo que debes saber al respecto. A través del Decreto Supremo n.º 020-2026-TR, el Gobierno estableció días no laborables entre el 11 al 16 de noviembre para Lima, Callao, Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque, Piura, Cusco y Ucayali, con motivo a la visita del papa León XIV. Esta medida es compensable y se rige por normas distintas a las de los feriados. Es decir, en el sector público, las horas no laboradas deben recuperarse dentro de los diez días posteriores o en el plazo que establezca cada entidad. En tanto, en el sector privado, empleadores y trabajadores pueden acordar la forma de compensar esas horas. Si no llegan a un consenso, el empleador determina las condiciones para su recuperación. Por consiguiente, te presentamos, compartido por Infobae, los departamentos en las que regirá estos días de descanso: 11 de noviembre: 12 de noviembre: 13 de noviembre: 14 de noviembre: 15 de noviembre: 16 de noviembre: Durante su visita al Perú, el papa León XIV participará en una vigilia de oración junto a miles de jóvenes de entre 16 y 35 años, que se realizará el jueves 12 de noviembre, a las 6:00 p. m., en el Estadio Nacional. Asimismo, el lunes 16 presidirá la Santa Misa de clausura, programada para las 10:30 a. m. en la Base Aérea Las Palmas. Según los organizadores, los asistentes deberán contar con una entrada gratuita, que podrán obtener a través de las plataformas Teleticket y Ticketmaster. Sin embargo, quienes no puedan asistir a alguna de estas actividades por diversos motivos no podrán ceder su entrada a un familiar o ser querido, ya que los boletos son intransferibles y están vinculados a los datos personales registrados previamente por cada asistente, según informó el Arzobispado de Lima. Inclusive, indicaron que será indispensable presentar el documento de identidad en la puerta del recinto el día del evento, garantizando que el acceso sea gratuito.

articles.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang? A highly unscientific list of possible successors | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Nvidia has no succession plan and a CEO in hot water, so we’ve drafted a shortlist.
articles.body_text: It’s almost inconceivable that Nvidia would fire its rock star CEO. Yet here we are, on the precipice of this happening. Over at Kalshi, Jensen Huang’s odds of surviving the week are sitting at a lowly 30% . Even though he built one of the world’s most valuable — and, many would argue, dangerously powerful — companies, the tides have completely turned against him. He has confessed to an extramarital affair, but as of Wednesday afternoon it isn’t even clear whom he meant: Alice Huang, the Chinese executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of spying for her country, or Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reports to him and who, five sources told The New York Times in an explosive new report, was also a paramour. Even if Huang is pushed out as CEO, the board members he has made very rich are unlikely to cut him loose entirely. Barring another shoe dropping, they could keep him on as chairman, a role Nvidia doesn’t currently have. But someone still has to run the company, and there’s no apparent succession plan, which leaves us, like everyone else, to speculate while we wait to see what happens next. While Huang’s 60 direct reports undoubtedly get a closer look, consider this our own parlor game, featuring some obvious and less obvious candidates: Lisa Su . The AMD CEO runs Nvidia’s most credible rival, as well as a distant cousin of Huang. The Information floated her name this week, but why would she leave her job for his? Her company stands to benefit from every day that Nvidia spends distracted by an investigation, congressional briefings, and all the mini dramas that are sure to follow. Her best move might be to send a nice note and keep her current corner office. Eric Schmidt. He was the pick of Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management, who we talked with earlier this week. Schmidt could “parachute in tomorrow and do a very good job,” Sonnenfeld said, and perhaps he could. He ran Google from 2001 to 2011, chaired the National Security Commission on AI from 2018 to 2021, and now runs the rocket company Relativity Space. Chips, software, government, rockets — it’s an impressive range. Then again, Schmidt would bring a lot of baggage when it comes to his own extramarital dalliances . It’s hard to see him clearing the board for that reason. Lip-Bu Tan . Intel’s CEO knows chips, and right now he might welcome a very soft landing. Last month, Intel reported third-quarter revenue up 21% to $16.5 billion, then warned its fourth-quarter results would fall short of Wall Street’s forecasts. The AI boom has caused a memory-chip shortage, pushing up PC prices and cutting PC sales. That’s hurt Intel (PC chips are a big part of its business), and its stock plunged 20% in after-hours trading on the warning, having already slid more than 30% since September. A move to a company that’s eating everyone’s lunch would be a pretty amazing escape hatch. Bret Taylor. The former Salesforce co-CEO and OpenAI board chair now runs the AI startup Sierra, and his resume includes a lot of the biggest brands in Silicon Valley. He co-created Google Maps, served as Facebook’s CTO, and chaired Twitter’s board through its sale to Elon Musk. He then took over as OpenAI’s board chair after the “Blip,” Sam Altman’s firing and fast return. When companies need an unflappable, likable adult in the room, they call Taylor. He probably knows nearly every customer Nvidia has, too. Ian Buck. If the board feels strongly about having a “builder” at the helm, they could do worse than the Nvidia VP who helped develop CUDA, the chip software that has become central to Nvidia’s dominance in AI. Analysts and former employees have floated him as a possible successor, and Kalshi traders give him a middling shot . He’s no household name, but the Stanford PhD seems more viable if Huang can can keep that chairman title and push for a successor he can work with. Someone else down the hall. Andrew Bell, Nvidia’s senior vice president of hardware engineering, arrived 25 years ago as a fresh Cornell grad and has been on an upward trajectory at the company ever since. Like Buck and dozens of other executives who are presumably being scrutinized, he reports directly to Huang. Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is the insider most often named, but analysts say she isn’t necessarily a natural successor as an innovator and visionary, and Bell has the chip pedigree. The wild card? Lori Huang . Nobody has floated her, but hear us out: Jensen met his wife as lab partners at Oregon State, so she has been working with him since before Nvidia existed. After graduating, she worked at Silicon Graphics as a micro chip engineer (making more money than her husband, he has said), then scaled back to raise the couple’s family, and she now co-leads the family trusts. If the board wants continuity, they could do worse than a humbler Huang who is also a brainiac. There’s a reason they say that behind every great man is a great woman (and vice versa). articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The affair could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
articles.body_text: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, the Times has reported. The story took a sudden new turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. Separately, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust Huang , and Nvidia’s shares fell in after-hours trading. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per the Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days. Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said . The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan. The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO. According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year. Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressman to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China committee Chairman Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed .

articles.summary: Jensen Huang, who has come under fire for admitting to an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent, has been accused of having a separate affair with an Nvidia subordinate.
articles.body_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is already under investigation after having admitted to having an affair with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy . Like many companies, Nvidia has rules discouraging superiors from having relationships with employees in subordinate roles, the Times notes. TechCrunch reached out to Nvidia for comment. The company’s board has initiated an investigation into Huang’s publicly admitted affair. Additionally, two House Republicans said Wednesday that Congress is gearing up to subpoena Huang over the spy allegations if he doesn’t voluntarily respond to their summons to a closed-door briefing. Late Wednesday, after the reports of the second affair were published, the Wall Street Journal reported that the Nvidia board was preparing to oust Huang, who co-founded the company in 1993. articles.title: CoreWeave turns to customer prepayments, shorter contracts to fund AI growth | TechCrunch
articles.summary: CoreWeave is increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even looking to short-term deals that could lead to higher prices, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings.
articles.body_text: CoreWeave is rewriting how it pays for the AI boom, according to the company’s third-quarter earnings , reported on Tuesday. CoreWeave, a neocloud that rents out the computing power behind AI, said it’s increasingly asking customers to pay up front, borrowing against specific contracts, and even pursuing short-term deals that could lead to higher prices. The new strategies could help CoreWeave finance its growth more efficiently while squeezing more cash from existing infrastructure. But these bets only hold if today’s demand and pricing power continue. CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in revenue, up 168% from the year prior, but it also posted a $709 million net loss and $846 million in quarterly interest expense. “We will not use the unsecured debt market to fund our business at current yields, nor do we need to,” CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said during Tuesday’s earnings call. Instead, CoreWeave’s plan is to rely on loans backed by specific customer contracts, drawing on funds as needed to finance most of the infrastructure it still has to build to deliver on its significant backlog of $132.5 billion. CoreWeave also said it expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months, including more than $3 billion tied to signing new customer contracts for capacity it has already built, which requires no additional spending on hardware. Rivals Nebius and IREN have also relied on hefty Microsoft prepayments to pay for computing capacity, signaling that the industry is moving toward asking Big Tech to pay up for their buildouts. Upfront payments could alleviate CoreWeave’s immediate borrowing needs, but they also commit the company to providing services at a price that might be less attractive down the road if compute demand continues to surge. CoreWeave is also looking to capitalize on that growing demand by signing more shorter-term contracts that can command much higher prices. The company raised prices across its offerings by about 25% in July and by another 10% later in the quarter. Prices are still climbing this quarter, in a way that “more than offset[s] cost increases,” said Intrator. “We are also allocating more capacity to short-term opportunities, where the pricing justifies it, selling capacity at more than $40 million per megawatt annually, while pricing for new infrastructure on four- and five-year contracts is moving to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt,” the chief executive said. CoreWeave’s financing strategy now revolves around those opportunities. In August, the company closed a $2.6 billion loan, its first designed specifically for shorter-term customer contracts. Known as DDTL 5.5, it lets CoreWeave borrow in installments as it needs the money.

articles.title: OpenAI's quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sales of $10 billion represents an almost 50% jump from revenue of $6.7 billion the company recorded in the second quarter.
articles.body_text: OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported , citing anonymous sources. If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year. OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said. OpenAI, one of the first to commercialize AI models, wasn’t exactly struggling to continue growing its top-line expansion — 18% growth on top of $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue is massive by any measure, especially compared to most software businesses. Still, the company lagged Anthropic in catering to enterprises, a market where the Claude maker has pulled ahead, at least in terms of revenue growth. OpenAI has recently benefited from a combination of tighter pricing, discounts, improving models, and a greater focus on building more enterprise-focused products and AI agents that can help people complete tasks. OpenAI has now reached an annual revenue run rate of $50 billion, according to Bloomberg. Meanwhile, Anthropic, which is seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation in an IPO likely to happen soon , said yesterday that its annual revenue run rate had increased by $10 billion within a month to $81 billion as of the end of October. (Note that OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently: Anthropic counts sales made by its cloud partners, while OpenAI only reports its share of some sales through its partners.) None of those figures are small, of course, but the companies are also competing with models from Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, as well as a plethora of cheaper but still highly capable models from open source AI labs, especially those from China. articles.title: Siri co-founder backs Helix for its voice ID tech | TechCrunch
articles.summary: With the rise of AI agents like Instinct and Muse, the industry needs to rethink human identity on the internet and rely on biometric signals like voice, which is where Helix comes in.
articles.body_text: For years, websites have relied on technology like CAPTCHA to prove that the user on the other end is human. More recently, social media platforms have turned to photos or videos to verify users’ identities. Now, a startup called Helix is betting that voice technology can do the same job, without requiring users to hand over sensitive personal information. The voice technology, which can run directly on a user’s device, has attracted backing from Siri co-founder Dag Kittlaus, who will also act as an adviser. The company raised $6.2 million in funding in a round led by Chicago Ventures, with participation from BAM Ventures, Aglaé Ventures, Corazon Capital, Press On Ventures, Tusk Ventures, Yonder Ventures, Rule 30, and Brown Angel Group. The startup was founded by Alex Oberg, Anna Dorofiyenko, and Mike Hall in 2025. Oberg previously worked at Ticketmaster, which acquired his startup; Dorofiyenko led data science teams at Live Nation and Zillow; and Hall has worked at Nike and Tinder, where he helped develop the initial matching algorithm. At Ticketmaster, Oberg played a role in creating Verified Fan, which is designed to keep bots out of the platform. As AI advanced, he started thinking along the same lines for a new solution. “As AI started to come up in the last two years, I was realizing that it’s going to make it increasingly difficult to determine who’s human and who’s not on the internet. Identity on the internet’s always been about proxies for identity, right? It’s your email, it’s your phone, it’s your IP address, it’s your device fingerprint, it’s your device ID,” Oberg said. He noted that with the rise of AI agents like Instinct and Muse, the industry needs to rethink human identity on the internet and rely on biometric signals like voice, which is where Helix comes in. Its core technology can run directly on a device to determine whether someone is human and estimate their age. The company is also running pilots to explore whether voice can be used as a biomarker to detect conditions such as drunkenness or distress. The company can deploy its technology to replace or supplement CAPTCHA and help block bot attacks. Helix said that because its model can run locally even on an iPhone 13, the cost of deploying the technology is minimal. The startup said one of its customers is Zeel, an in-home healthcare provider that uses Helix’s tech to verify the identities of providers visiting customers’ homes. The CEO also emphasized the limitations of Helix’s technology, noting that it cannot reliably detect whether someone is lying. He added that its voice technology doesn’t identify individual speakers — while verifying them being unique humans — and claimed that even if the company stores a voiceprint, it cannot be used to reconstruct a person’s voice. AI-powered fraud is also a growing problem in phone calls. But Helix believes its technology isn’t yet capable of reliably detecting AI agents during live calls. Siri co-founder Kittlaus said that voice-identification technology has finally reached a point where it works reliably, positioning Helix to scale as AI-powered fraud increases. He also said that Helix’s work to compress its models gives the startup a cost advantage.

articles.title: Databricks' new AI agent tells CEO Ali Ghodsi the unvarnished truth | TechCrunch
articles.summary: With Databricks at 12,000 employees, AI Ghodsi is the first to admit that he can't know everyone and that they are unlikely to confess the things that go wrong to him. But he doesn't need them to. He uses Databricks' newly revised Genie agent for that.
articles.body_text: Databricks on Wednesday unveiled an updated version of its AI agent Genie, which can now perform multistep jobs that take extended work to finish. It does this through an ontology that Databricks built to give Genie the context it needs from the information that customers store on the Databricks platform. Corporate leaders can now assign the agent a wide range of tasks, and it will complete them unsupervised, the company says. To prove the point, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi showed me how he uses it internally. Instead of a product demo, he fired up his actual agent and walked me through his most recent chats and charts. He showed me how it analyzed the parts of an employee satisfaction survey where the company didn’t score well, and how it helped him rate (and discard) fixes for those low scores that some executives suggested. He showed me how it summarized a big sales pitch to a prospect that went poorly — including the features the prospect said it needed before buying. It also prepped him for a podcast interview by reviewing his previous appearances and developing likely questions. While we talked, he even had it tell him what he should say to me. (And its advice on that wasn’t bad.) The fascinating part was that Ghodsi was using Genie to find the stuff that he’s now unlikely to hear as the big boss. It was a source of unvarnished truth about what wasn’t going well that he needed to address. “Have you heard of Dunbar’s number? The magic number is 150,” he said when I pointed this out. Named for British anthropologist Robin Dunbar, it’s theoretically the maximum number of people with whom humans can maintain stable relationships. In a small startup, a CEO knows everyone, has direct relationships with them, and they feel safe to tell him negative info straight up. With 12,000 employees, Ghodsi is the first to admit he can’t know everyone. At that size, a salesperson isn’t likely to confess a disastrous sales call to the CEO. An HR manager isn’t likely to confess that their idea for increasing employee satisfaction will probably fail. “Anyone who has more than 150 employees, which is a lot of companies, a lot of people can get value out of this,” he said of AI agents generally and his product, Genie, specifically. Ghodsi’s own use of Genie (often called dogfooding, from the phrase “eating your own dogfood”) is one reason why Databricks is now pitching it as an always-on agent for business leaders. He says he also uses it in his personal life, rather than a security-questionable alternative like OpenClaw or Instinct or Muse. He believes Genie can do for the business side what AI, agents, and harnesses (the software that wraps around an AI model and lets it use tools) are doing for programmers. As for the risk that agents will ratchet up corporate AI costs, Ghodsi has an answer for that, too. He said costs can be controlled through Databricks’ Unity Gateway product.
